title: Latency-centric opportunistic phase-consolidation scheduler
creator: Maya Chen
description: Goal: design and validate a scheduler that opportunistically consolidates short prefill phases into bounded batches while preserving tenant-level fairness and minimizing end-to-end prefill+decode tail latency. Background: many requests exhibit a 'micro-prefill' pattern (short prefill followed by short decode) that produces high scheduling overhead and tail latency when treated with coarse phase boundaries. The Phase-Consolidation Scheduler (PCS) uses soft-deadlines, phase coalescing windows, and a utility function to decide when to merge adjacent prefill work into a single execution unit. PCS aims to reduce amortized kernel setup and attention kernel warmup cost, increase GPU utilization for short sequences, and avoid starving long-running decodes. Key behaviors: 1) Phase bucketing: classify requests into micro, standard, and long prefill buckets based on token estimates and recent traffic. 2) Consolidation window: a short, configurable window (default 10ms) where micro-prefill requests can be grouped and dispatched together if utility improves. 3) Soft-deadline hedging: requests close to latency SLOs may be hedged to a fast-path kernel or sent to a dedicated low-latency lane. 4) Utility-based arbitration: scheduler computes a utility score per candidate consolidation that balances expected latency improvement, throughput gain, and estimated fairness impact (tenant-penalty term). 5) Fairness normalization: tenant budgets and recent service variance are folded into the utility to avoid consolidation biasing heavy tenants. Interaction with runtime: PCS signals preferred kernel variants (e.g., packed-attn fast-path vs quantized long-seq kernels) to the kernel selection layer and requests KV-cache warmups where beneficial. Implementation plan: prototype in the scheduler simulation harness, run trace-driven simulations on 3 months of production traffic, then implement a canary scheduler on staging GPUs with traffic shadowing. Success metrics: P50/P95 prefill+decode latency reduction for micro-prefill flows, throughput delta, fairness delta (Gini coefficient over per-tenant latency SLO violations), GPU kernel occupancy, and added scheduler CPU overhead. Risks and trade-offs: consolidation window too long increases tail latency for interactive flows; tenant fairness tuning is sensitive and may require an SLA-aware knob; extra CPU scheduling cost could offset GPU runtime gains for low-load hosts. Rollout strategy: roll out as a toggleable scheduler module behind runtime feature-flag, start with internal tenants and then opt-in customers. Links: design doc https://confluence.redwood.internal/pages/PCS-Design, prototype PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/3987
comments: 2025-11-04 Maya Chen: Initial RFC and motivating traces uploaded to Confluence. Called out micro-prefill distribution and kernel warmup penalty in analysis.
2025-11-18 Design review: PM and Kernel team suggested exposing a per-tenant consolidation budget to prevent cross-tenant amplification. Added tenant-penalty term to utility function.

2026-01-15 Simulation run v1: 3-month trace replay showed 18% P95 reduction for micro-prefill flows but a 2% increase in P95 for long-decode-heavy tenants at high load. Tuned consolidation window and tenant-weighting.
2026-02-02 Prototype PR opened: runtime/scheduler: add phase bucketing, consolidation window, and utility arbitration. PR #3987 links to benchmark harness. Reviewers: @karim, @sloane.

2026-02-20 Staging A/B results (shadowing): P50 latency -6ms for interactive chat flows, P95 -22ms on micro-prefill cohort. GPU occupancy improved by ~9%. Observed 0.4% increase in scheduler CPU cycles on control plane hosts.

2026-03-10 Engineering sync: agreed on canary plan, safety knobs (per-tenant disable, max-consolidation-size), and automated rollback thresholds (P95 regression >5% for any tenant). Next: implement telemetry to surface per-tenant consolidation events and fairness histograms.
